translations.answer: Yes. PR #1570 adds rw_rate to each ros2_control hardware component and updates the official documentation, parsing/scheduling implementation, and testing. The documentation example shows system, actuator, and sensor running at 500/200/250 Hz respectively; if not set, it follows controller_manager, and if higher, it only runs at controller_manager rate.
translations.applicability: Applies to versions containing PR #1570; whether the release package has been reverted needs separate confirmation.
translations.credibility.rationale: The issue has been closed, the environment is clear and there is no conflict, and there is formal documentation or precise reference to an independent replication.
translations.details.attempts.0: PR #1570 adds rw_rate to each hardware component.
translations.details.attempts.1: Maintainer suggests using counter/internal filtering to skip low-frequency voltage readings within a component, or splitting components.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: First determine if different frequency signals can be assigned to different ros2_control hardware components.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Distinguish between controller update rate, hardware component rw_rate, and the actual sampling rate of each state within a component.
translations.details.diagnostics.2: Expose timestamp or staleness of states used for reusing old values to prevent controllers from treating cached values as new samples.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Across components: set rw_rate in ros2_control tag; actual rate is limited by controller_manager rate when higher.
translations.details.effective_fixes.1: Same component: update target state with counter/filter rules for low-frequency readings, skip periodic retention of previous values; or restructure into separate components.
translations.details.environments.0: ros2_control rolling/master period; PR #1570 has been merged; specific ROS 2 release version needs to be checked for backport.
translations.details.limits.0: PR #1570 corresponds to the parameter name and semantics of the merge version; different ROS 2 release versions need verification.
translations.details.limits.1: The counter scheme for the same component is a maintainer's suggestion; no thread has been published with deployment testing.
translations.details.outcomes.0: Component-level rw_rate has been merged and documented/tested; fine-grained interface for sub-state of state being updated by controller is not yet implemented in this thread.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: How to configure different read/write rates for multiple hardware components?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: How to avoid reading low-frequency signals when position is 100 Hz and voltage is 0.1/1 Hz within a single hardware component?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: When reusing old values, carry timestamp/validity and set timeout; expired temperature, voltage, or fault states should not be silently used for safety decisions.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Fixed high-frequency read/write will cause low-frequency states to consume bandwidth, leading to retries, packet loss, and extra delay.
translations.source.locator: ros2_control #649 maintainer's comment pointing to PR #1570; merged documentation, implementation, and testing for PR #1570
translations.source.title: ros2_control multi-rate needs to distinguish component-level rw_rate from internal signal throttling within a component
translations.title: Does ros2_control already have a formal mechanism for different read/write rates for hardware components?
